battle.name: 雁門之圍
battle.brief: 大業十一年，隋煬帝征高句麗敗回師，車駕次雁門，突厥始畢可汗率約二十萬騎兵合圍雁門城，城中兵民十五萬口，存糧僅支二十日。守軍憑城頭弩弓與拒馬抵禦騎兵衝鋒，靠大臣出使議和、始畢可汗撤圍而罷。卡面希臘重步兵方陣雖與本役相隔千餘年，其互相遮蔽、強化正面的原理，正是守城步卒對付騎兵的依托。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 大業十一年（615）秋，隋朝與東突厥汗國在雁門城內外正面對峙。隋方不是一支專門為守城組建的部隊，而是隋煬帝西巡的整個御營：天子、隨駕百官、宮掖衛士與大批官民隨從都滯在雁門城中，兵力的骨幹是武衛與殿內宿衛，以及各州郡抽調來的郡兵與府兵殘部。指揮系統由天子自任總帥，兵部與尚書省調度文書，宿衛將軍掌城防，各州郡自報兵員、由郡守縣令領軍，地方指揮極度分散。北方各鎮因連年用兵高句麗與山東，流民未安，郡兵多數空缺，雁門這樣的邊關重鎮常駐兵力極少。突厥一方以始畢可汗為首，兵馬約二十萬騎（《資治通鑑》等作「數十萬」），由汗庭直接指揮，部眾分屬始畢、頡利、突利等不同部落；他們沒有足以攻破隋代夯土城牆的攻城器械，卻擁有草原式的機動與投射優勢。兩國關係在開皇年間曾靠互市與和親維持，到大業年間已轉為邊境衝突與互攻，本役即是大規模戰爭前夜隋朝北疆的一次全面試探。
countriesEn: In the autumn of 615, the eleventh year of the Daye era, the Sui dynasty and the Eastern Turkic Khaganate stood face to face inside and outside the walls of Yanmen. The Sui side was not a force raised for the purpose of holding a city, but the entire travelling encampment of Emperor Yang of Sui: the Son of Heaven, the hundreds of officials who travelled with him, the palace guards and a great mass of civil and military followers were all penned inside Yanmen, and the backbone of its fighting strength was the Wuwei and dian-nei imperial guards together with remnants of the fubing regiments and of the county levies drawn in from the various prefectures. The command system was centred on the emperor as commander-in-chief himself, the Ministry of War and the Department of State Affairs handling the written orders, the guards commanders taking charge of the walls, while each prefecture reported its own numbers of men and the prefects and magistrates led them — local command was extremely dispersed. The northern garrisons had been drained by years of campaigning against Goguryeo and in Shandong, the displaced peasants had not yet been resettled, most county levies stood vacant, and a strategic border fortress such as Yanmen ordinarily held very few men. On the Turkic side the host was under Shibi Khan in person, some two hundred thousand horsemen (the Zizhi Tongjian and other works give 'several hundred thousand'), commanded directly from the khagan's court, its warriors drawn from separate tribes — Shibi's own, Jieli's, Tuli's and others. They had no siege engines capable of breaking a rammed-earth Sui wall, but they possessed the mobility and the reach of the steppe. Between the two states, relations had rested on frontier trade and marriage alliances during the Kaihuang era; by the Daye era they had already degenerated into border clashes and mutual raids, and this siege was a complete probing of the Sui's northern frontier on the eve of a general war.
people: 雁門之圍把隋煬帝、突厥可汗與一整批將相同時推到聚光燈下。隋煬帝楊廣在第二次征高句麗失敗後巡遊北邊，途中被圍；據《資治通鑑》，城頭流矢曾射到御前，他抱著幼子趙王楊杲落淚，哭到眼睛腫起，此後數日不敢獨自在城頭露面。主持守城的是武衛大將軍樊子蓋，他整飭軍令、分段布防、穩住隨駕官民，後來又奉命出關平定敬盤陀、柴保昌之亂。御史大夫虞世基力主不要與突厥硬拼，催請遣使議和；民部尚書裴矩與虞世基同赴突厥營中交涉，憑城中存糧與形勢說動始畢可汗退兵，裴矩此後以安撫邊境、經略西域與降服吐谷渾著稱。始畢可汗的配偶是隋宗室女義成公主，她久居突厥牙中，議和時從中轉圜；可汗死後她歸隋，入唐後封虢國夫人。可汗之弟頡利可汗在漠南另領一部，兄弟之間的裂痕，幾年後成為隋唐在漠南角力的破口。城外還有各地陸續趕來的郡兵與被徵發的民夫，他們大多被突厥遊騎擋在城外，未能形成有效的解圍力量；而城內隨駕的百官與家屬，既是城中十五萬口的大半，也是糧食最先耗盡的一部分。
peopleEn: The siege of Yanmen pushed Emperor Yang of Sui, the Turkic khagan and a whole company of generals and ministers into the full glare of history. Yang Guang, having failed in his second campaign against Goguryeo, was touring the northern frontier when he was surrounded; the Zizhi Tongjian records that arrows from the walls reached the imperial position, and that he broke down in tears while holding his young son, Prince Zhao Yang Gao, his eyes swollen with weeping, and that for several days afterwards he did not dare show his face alone on the ramparts. The defence of the city was directed by the Wuwei general Fan Zigae, who straightened out the military discipline, organised the walls into sectors and steadied the officials and civilians who had followed the emperor; he was later sent out of the passes to put down the rising of Jing Pantuo and Chai Baochang. The Censor-in-chief Yu Shiji pressed for negotiation rather than a stand-up fight with the Turks and urged that envoys be sent out. The Minister of Revenue Pei Ju went with him into the Turkic camp and, by citing the grain in the city and the shape of the situation, persuaded Shibi Khan to withdraw; Pei Ju later became famous for pacifying the frontier, managing the western regions and bringing the Tuyuhun to terms. The khan's wife was a Sui princess by clan, Yicheng, who had long lived in the Turkic camp and who mediated during the settlement; after the khan's death she returned to Sui, and when that dynasty fell she entered the Tang and was made Lady of Guo. The khan's brother, Jieli, commanded a separate division in the desert north, and the rift between the brothers would a few years later become the crack through which Sui and Tang fought over the steppe. Outside the walls, county levies and conscripted labourers kept arriving from the various provinces but were held off by the Turkic light horse and the main body, so that no effective relief force ever assembled. Inside, the officials and their households who had followed the emperor were both the greater part of the 150,000 souls in the city and the first portion of the population to exhaust the grain.
kits: 卡面是希臘重步兵方陣：圓盾 aspis，青銅包邊蒙皮，直徑約一公尺；長槍 dory，長約一點八至二公尺；胸甲有青銅胸鎧與亞麻疊層的 linothorax；頭戴科林斯式青銅盔，脛甲護腿，另配短劍 xiphos。公元前五世紀的方陣縱深僅四至八排，亞歷山大大軍把它加厚到八排、其後更增至十六排，前排跪或半跪、槍尖平舉，後排槍從肩上斜出。希臘人靠的不是個人勇力，而是盾牌接在一起形成的遮蔽：左側由身後同袍的盾與身體覆蓋，進攻時全陣向右微微旋轉，把右肩與右側的盾緣讓出來，使後排能投槍與刺擊；卡面那句「盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實」，說的就是這個原理。雁門城頭當然沒有希臘重步兵，隋軍的裝備是弓弩（擘張弩與臂弓）、矢石、投石用的飛石與石砲、封閉缺口用的拒馬與鹿角，另有明光鎧、兜鍪、槊、矛與其他鎧甲；糧秣只夠二十日，連騾馬的飼料都成了難題。但同一套原理在中國兵書裏以另一種樣貌存在：以長兵與拒馬結成的方陣，以及唐人所稱的「車牆」，用車箱圍成環形或方形，戰士以長槊從車隙中刺出，用以抵擋騎兵衝鋒。隋末淺水灘之役，隋軍以大車結方陣進逼，卻被高句麗的奇兵襲其陣後而致崩潰，說明車陣能擋正面、卻怕被繞側；而唐人談車陣禦騎，重點仍放在不開缺口、以長兵封住正面。希臘方陣與中國車陣相隔一千一百餘年，器械與戰法全不相同，要回答的卻是同一個問題：面對速度與衝力，密集步兵怎樣把個人的脆弱換成整體的堅硬。
kitsEn: The card shows the Greek hoplite phalanx: the round aspis shield, edged in bronze and faced with hide, roughly a metre across; the long spear, the dory, about 1.8 to 2 metres in length; body armour of either a bronze corselet or layered linen, the linothorax; the Corinthian bronze helmet; greaves for the lower legs; and a short sword, the xiphos. The phalanx of the fifth century BC stood only four to eight files deep; Alexander's army thickened it to eight and later to sixteen, the front rank kneeling or half-kneeling with the spear points level, the rear ranks bringing their spears down over the shoulders. What the Greeks relied on was not individual valour but the shading that came from shields locked together: the left side of a man was covered by the shield and body of the man behind him, and when attacking the whole formation rotated slightly to the right, giving up the right shoulder and the rim of the right-hand shield so that the rear ranks could throw and thrust. The line on the card — that when shields are joined together the front of an army is stronger than a single man — states exactly this principle. There were of course no Greek hoplites on the ramparts of Yanmen. The Sui defences were bows and crossbows, including the high-tension crossbow and the ordinary bow, together with arrows and stones, the flying stones and stone throwers used to hurl missiles, and the cheval-de-frise and deer-horn obstacles used to seal every gap, plus the shining plate cuirass, the helmet, the long sao-pike, the lance and other armour. Grain would last twenty days only, and even the fodder for the pack animals had become a problem. Yet the same principle existed in Chinese military literature in another guise: the square formation closed with long weapons and cheval-de-frise, and the formation built out of wagons that the Tang called the che qiang, a ring or a square of wagons with the spears of the infantry pushed out through the gaps, deployed to absorb the charge of horse. At the shallows in 613 the Sui advanced in just such a wagon formation and broke up when Goguryeo's light troops struck its rear, showing that a wagon wall can hold the front yet fears being turned; and the Tang discussions of the wagon formation against horsemen put the same emphasis on never opening a gap and on sealing the front with long weapons. The Greek phalanx and the Chinese wagon formation are separated by more than eleven centuries and share neither equipment nor method, yet they answer the same question: facing speed and impact, how does a dense infantry body exchange the fragility of individuals for the hardness of a whole.
tactics: 突厥的圍城是一套草原式的部署。約二十萬騎分作幾種任務：合圍城垣的主體、往返巡邏切斷出入的遊騎，以及一部份逼近御營施壓逼迫議和的突騎。他們沒有足以對付夯土城牆的攻城塔與重型投石機，因此多採圍而不攻：射覆城頭與街道、切斷糧道、搜掠周邊村落、把援軍擋在城外。試探性的衝鋒只用來測定城門守備、箭雨密度與守軍反擊的時機，一旦城頭反擊得力就立刻退開，因為對草原騎兵而言，損失一批坐騎與乘手的代價遠高於多攻一日。隋軍的守城則是把城頭切成若干段，每段配弓弩手、射手與拒馬，射界互相交疊，凡馬匹可以衝上的門面、坡道與缺口，一律以鹿角、拒馬與坑塹封死；出城反擊只取夜裡或拂曉，派小股步騎焚燒敵營、破壞其包圍部署，試圖在圍圈上撕開缺口，而不是在城門外列陣與二十萬騎兵決鬥。守方還得同時處理糧食：存糧只夠二十日，隨駕的官民與騾馬同樣要吃，於是節糧、徵集城中存糧、嚴禁官吏私下買賣，成為城務的一部分；而各地郡兵與義勇雖陸續抵達，卻被遊騎隔在城外，援軍實際上不存在。希臘方陣可以作為守城的對照：亞歷山大大軍的方陣縱深加到十六排，進攻時全陣向右旋轉、以右肩讓出投槍與刺擊的空間；防禦時則靠密度與不移動，讓整個正面始終比任何一名戰士更難突破。雁門城頭沒有方陣，但「用排列換取強度」這一點，正是當日守軍面對萬騎時唯一能用的辦法。外交通訊與議和是這場戰鬥的延伸：城中的存糧數目被如實擺上桌面，朝廷以賄遺與姻好換取退兵，最終靠一次外交交易而不是一場決戰解了圍。
tacticsEn: The Turkic investment of the city followed a steppe pattern of deployment. The two hundred thousand horsemen were divided among several tasks: the main body closing the circuit of the walls, light horse patrolling in circles to cut the entrances and exits, and a detachment pressing close to the imperial camp to force a settlement. Lacking siege towers and heavy stone-throwers sufficient against a rammed-earth wall, they generally chose to surround rather than to assault: they swept the ramparts and the streets with arrows, cut the grain road, ravaged the villages round about, and held the relieving forces off outside. Their probing charges were used only to measure the guarding of the gates, the density of the arrow rain and the timing of the defenders' counter-stroke; as soon as a counter-stroke from the walls told well they withdrew again, since for steppe cavalry the loss of a batch of mounts and riders cost far more than one more day of siege. The Sui defence cut the walls into a number of sectors, each with bowmen, crossbowmen and cheval-de-frise, their fields of fire interlocking; every gate front, ramp and breach over which a horse might charge was sealed with deer-horn obstacles, cheval-de-frise and ditches. Their counter-strokes were launched by night or at dawn, small bodies of foot and horse setting fire to the enemy camp and breaking up the encirclement, trying to tear a gap in the ring rather than to line up outside the gates and fight a mass of cavalry in open battle. The defenders had to handle the grain at the same time: twenty days' supply only, the officials and civilians of the convoy and the mules and horses all had to eat, so rationing, requisitioning the grain in the city and forbidding private dealing by the officials became part of the city's administration, while the county levies and volunteers who did arrive were held outside by the light horse, so that in truth there was no relieving army. The Greek phalanx serves as a comparison for such a defence: Alexander's formation was deepened to sixteen files, and when attacking the whole body rotated to the right, giving up the right shoulder so that the rear ranks could throw and thrust; in defence it relied on density and on standing still, so that the whole front was always harder to break than any single warrior. There was no phalanx on the walls of Yanmen, but the one idea available to a garrison facing twenty thousand riders was exactly this — to buy strength with arrangement.
data: 可用的數字不多，但有幾個是明確的。圍城一方的兵力，突厥方面記為約二十萬騎，《資治通鑑》等史書亦有「數十萬」之說，兩說相差頗大，取二十萬較為穩妥。城內一方的數目是「兵民十五萬口」，這是隨駕官民與守軍的總數，真正能上城頭作戰的只有武衛宿衛與郡兵中的數千人，餘者多是被捲入的隨行人口。存糧的數字最為具體：僅可支二十日，說明遠在援軍指望之前，雁門城已接近斷糧的門檻。時間上，圍城自九月開始，至十月、十一月間得解，前後約一個多月；這段時間內各地調來的郡兵與義勇陸續抵達，卻被突厥遊騎與正面大軍隔在城外，未能形成有效的解圍力量。地理上，雁門關地處太行山北麓的孔道，南距晉陽（今太原）沿山道約二百公里，正當北去雲中、馬邑與南入太原的交通要衝，控扼此處便能卡斷巡幸隊伍的退路。卡面那支希臘方陣的尺度也可對照：aspis 圓盾直徑約一公尺，dory 長槍約一點八至二公尺，後來更長的 sarissa 可達四至六公尺；亞歷山大大軍的方陣前排約二十五人、縱深八排，其後加到十六排，方陣正面寬約一百公尺上下，重裝步兵的密度正足以讓箭矢在同一方向疊成一片難以穿越的牆。
dataEn: There are not many usable figures, but several of them are firm. The besieging force is recorded on the Turkic side as about 200,000 horsemen, though the Zizhi Tongjian and other histories also give 'several hundred thousand'; the two estimates differ considerably, and 200,000 is the more cautious reading. On the side inside the city the figure is '150,000 soldiers and civilians', a total covering the travelling officials and people together with the garrison; the men who could actually fight from the walls were only several thousand of the guards and county levies, the rest being people swept along in the convoy. The figure for grain is the most precise of all: it would last twenty days only, which shows that Yanmen stood close to the threshold of famine long before any relieving army could be hoped for. As to time, the investment began in the ninth month and was lifted in the tenth or eleventh, a matter of a little over a month; during that stretch the county levies and volunteers sent from the various provinces arrived one after another but were held off by the Turkic light horse and the main body, so that no effective relief force was ever formed. As to geography, the fortress of Yanmen stands in a defile on the northern foot of the Taihang range; by mountain road it lies some 200 kilometres south of Jinyang, present-day Taiyuan, and it commands the traffic that runs north to Yunzhong and Mayi and south into the Taiyuan plain, so that holding it cut the retreat of the travelling column. The dimensions of the Greek phalanx on the card can be set beside these: the aspis was about a metre in diameter, the dory about 1.8 to 2 metres, and the longer sarissa that came later could reach four to six metres; the front rank of Alexander's formation was about twenty-five men deep at eight files and later sixteen, giving a frontage of roughly a hundred metres, a density of armoured infantry just sufficient to pile the arrows of one direction into a wall that could not be crossed.
cause: 雁門之圍不是偶發的遭遇，而是隋朝大業十一年一整套崩壞的必然結果。直接原因是邊防空虛：大業八年至十年三次征高句麗，兵役與丁役耗盡關中與各地的府兵與民夫，北方各鎮的郡兵多被抽調往遼東作戰；同年上半年朝廷又用兵山東，樊子蓋奉命出關討敬盤陀、柴保昌，關中精兵遠在千里之外。乘此空檔，東突厥始畢可汗以二十萬騎南下，選擇的正是隋煬帝巡幸北邊、回師必經的雁門孔道，企圖在皇帝與朝廷暴露於荒野的時候一舉擒獲。內部的失序更使情況惡化：615 年上半年，河北的魏騏驎、齊郡的顏宣政、涿郡的王須拔相繼起事，郡兵四處討伐，關中兵也被牽制，朝廷沒有任何一支可以自由調動的機動兵。遠因則是十多年來對高句麗用兵與巡遊天下帶來的國力消耗，以及大業年間對邊疆關係的處置失當：既未能穩住北邊，又未能真正壓服高句麗，反而把兩個方向的戰線同時拉開，兩邊都空著。煬帝本人輕敵冒進、認定突厥會像往年一樣避開御駕，是最後一個直接誘因。
causeEn: The siege of Yanmen was not a chance encounter but the necessary result of a whole structure falling apart in the eleventh year of the Daye era. The immediate cause was an empty frontier. The three campaigns against Goguryeo from 608 to 610 consumed the fubing levies and the labour of the peasants of Guanzhong and of every other region, and the county levies of the northern garrisons were mostly drawn off to the Liaodong front; in the first half of the same year the court was campaigning in Shandong as well, with Fan Zigae sent out of the passes against Jing Pantuo and Chai Baochang and the picked troops of Guanzhong thousands of li away. Into that gap the Eastern Turkic Shibi Khan marched south with 200,000 riders, choosing precisely the defile of Yanmen through which the touring emperor had to pass on his return, in the hope of seizing the emperor and the court while they lay exposed in the open country. The disorder inside the empire made matters worse: in the first half of 615 Wei Qilin rose in northern Zhili, Yan Xuanzheng rose at Licheng in Qizhou and Wang Xuba rose in Zhu Commandery of Youzhou, county levies were chasing them in every direction, the troops of Guanzhong were tied down as well, and the court possessed no force it could move freely. The deeper cause was the drain of national strength produced by more than a decade of war against Goguryeo and of tours of the realm, and the mishandling of the frontier in the Daye era: the north was never stabilised, nor was Goguryeo truly beaten down, and instead two fronts were opened at once with both of them hollow. That the emperor himself advanced rashly, expecting the Turks as in former years to keep out of the emperor's way, was the last direct inducement.
impact: 雁門之圍留下的不是一場決戰的勝負，而是一份制度體檢報告。它把隋朝北疆的真相攤在光天化日之下：號稱強盛的隋朝，能在雁門城頭站崗的只有數千宿衛與郡兵，北方重鎮的郡兵是空的，禁軍成了皇帝唯一能動用的力量。圍城之後，朝廷不得不靠天下募兵與臨時徵發來補防，把維持邊防的成本轉嫁給地方與百姓；募兵一旦成為常例，兵不再由均田農民輪番充任，而是由饑民與亡命之徒賣命充當，隋朝此後數年正是靠募兵、靠地方私募的武裝打平天下叛軍，而平叛的將領與武人集團也在這過程中坐大，府兵制崩解之後再也沒有重建。對北方而言，則把突厥的問題由邊患升級為執政難題：始畢可汗次年病死，頡利可汗與突利可汗兄弟相爭，619 年劉武周正是藉突厥的騎兵攻入太原、逼近長安，直到李靖在貞觀四年（630）奇襲定襄、貞觀年間大破頡利於陰山，才算把雁門欠下的帳收回來。義成公主在可汗死後歸隋，隋亡後入唐封虢國夫人，成為隋唐之間一段沒有斷開的人脈。對煬帝本人，這場圍城徹底拆毀了天子的威信：城頭的流矢射到御前、抱住幼子落淚的細節傳遍天下，天子被突厥圍在雁門的記憶，此後不斷被後人用來比擬新的危機。
impactEn: What the siege of Yanmen left behind was not the result of a decided battle but a physical examination of a system. It laid the truth about the Sui's northern frontier in the open: of a dynasty proclaimed strong, only several thousand guards and county levies could stand on the walls of Yanmen, the county levies of the northern strongholds were empty, and the imperial guard was the only force the emperor could move. After the siege the court had to fall back on recruiting volunteers from all over the realm and on emergency levies to shore up the frontier, passing the cost of defence on to the localities and to the people; once recruitment became the standing practice, soldiers were no longer peasants from the equal-field system serving in rotation but hungry men and runaways selling their lives, and the Sui spent the following years fighting the rebellions with recruited troops and with locally raised armed bands — and the generals and martial households who crushed those rebellions grew powerful in the process, so that the fubing system, once collapsed, was never rebuilt. On the northern front the siege turned a border raid into a problem of state: Shibi Khan died the following year, the brothers Jieli and Tuli disputed the succession, and in 619 Liu Wuzhou marched on Taiyuan with Turkic horse and came close to Chang'an; only Li Jing's night attack on Dingxiang in 630 and the crushing of Jieli at Yinshan in the Zhenguan years recovered the debt that Yanmen had left. Yicheng returned to Sui after the khan's death and, after the fall of that dynasty, entered the Tang as Lady of Guo, a human link between the two houses that never quite broke. For Yang Guang himself the siege destroyed the emperor's authority: the detail of the arrows from the walls reaching the imperial position and of a man weeping while holding his little son passed through the whole realm, and the memory of a Son of Heaven shut up in Yanmen by the Turks was used again and again afterwards to name new dangers.
result: 結局是城未破、圍解、人還。朝廷以厚賂相送、並許以互市與姻好，遣裴矩、虞世基出使議和，義成公主居中轉圜，始畢可汗終於解圍北還，隋煬帝得以率隊西行，雁門的守軍等來了援兵與糧食。代價卻真實存在：城中二十日的存糧在圍城期間被消耗殆盡，隨駕的馬匹大批餓斃，沿途州縣為大軍與馬匹供應而加派，牆垣堡寨在圍城與隨後的勤王軍事中被反覆消耗，修復的費用最終轉嫁到民間。對隋朝整體而言，雁門之圍是一次沒有輸家、只有延期的失敗——國家在制度上早已空虛，圍城只是把這份空虛暴露在北方邊境上。同年秋季起，天下兵亂此起彼伏：河北的魏騏驎、齊郡的顏宣政、涿郡的王須拔相繼舉兵，一年之內從山東到河間到燕地全線失控；募兵、屯糧、築城、討賊的開支又再抽一次民力。三年間，瓦崗軍、竇建德與李淵在隋末的廢墟上爭天下時，雁門的守軍早已等不到援兵。史家因此常把大業十一年視為隋朝由盛轉亡的轉折點：皇朝的軍隊尚在，帝國的筋骨已斷。
resultEn: The outcome was that the city was not taken, the siege was lifted, and the men came out. The court sent rich presents and promised trade and marriage ties; Pei Ju and Yu Shiji were sent out to treat, Yicheng mediated from within the Turkic camp, and Shibi Khan finally lifted the investment and went north again, so that the Sui emperor could lead his column west and the garrison of Yanmen at last saw relief and grain. The costs, though, were real: the twenty days of grain in the city were consumed to the last measure during the siege, a great many of the horses that travelled with the court starved, the prefectures along the route were charged with supplying the army and its animals, the walls and stockades of the frontier were battered and repaired again and again in the siege and in the campaigns that followed, and the bill for the repairs was passed on to the countryside. For the Sui as a whole the siege of Yanmen was a failure with no loser that was only postponed — the state had been hollow at the level of institutions for a long time, and the siege merely exposed that hollowness on the northern frontier. From the autumn of the same year rebellions flared up one after another: Wei Qilin in northern Zhili, Yan Xuanzheng at Licheng in Qizhou, Wang Xuba in Zhu Commandery of Youzhou, and within a single year the whole line from Shandong through Hebei to the Yan lands ran out of control; the costs of recruiting, storing grain, building walls and suppressing the risings drained the people once more. Within three years the Wagang army, Dou Jiande and Li Yuan were fighting over the ruins of the Sui, and the garrison of Yanmen had long since stopped waiting for relief. It is for this reason that historians so often treat the eleventh year of Daye as the turning point from strength to decline, when the dynasty still had its armies but the empire had lost the strength in its limbs.
